claims.text: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in the as-cast simple-solid-solution state has relatively low strength.
Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in the as-cast simple-solid-solution state has relatively low hardness.
Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in the as-cast simple-solid-solution state has high plasticity.
As-cast equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi is a homogeneous single-phase solid solution.
The as-cast CoCrFeNiTi solid solution has a random atomic distribution.
A lack of short-range chemical order causes the alloy's relatively low hardness and strength while permitting high plasticity.
Annealing near 700 °C with controlled slow cooling can induce short-range chemical order or nanoscale clustering in CoCrFeNiTi without producing secondary phases.
Short-range ordered regions generate local stresses or lattice distortions that impede dislocation glide.
A random atomic distribution provides minimal resistance to dislocation glide.
Annealing-induced short-range order will increase the hardness of CoCrFeNiTi relative to the as-cast alloy.
Annealing-induced short-range order will increase the yield strength of CoCrFeNiTi relative to the as-cast alloy.
The strengthening caused by short-range order will only moderately reduce ductility.
The hardness and strength improvement will be especially noticeable at room temperature.
The strength improvement will persist up to 600 °C but will be partly offset by thermally activated dislocation motion.
Annealing CoCrFeNiTi below about 800 °C avoids secondary-phase precipitation or gross microstructural changes.
The hypothesis is limited to single-phase equimolar CoCrFeNiTi tested from approximately 25 °C to 600 °C.
The applicable mechanical loads are near to, but do not exceed, the yield point.

contradictions.description: The stated loading boundary limits tests to loads not exceeding yield, but the proposed measurements include post-yield stress-strain behavior and ductility at failure, which require loading beyond yield.
